findings.message: The bug the fix was meant to remove (a second sighting arriving up to a whole interval late) still happens when two sightings are triggered on the same tick and the player has not yet used this snapshot's sighting. In packages/simulation/src/intel/step.ts, freeLead (lines 382-392) is called once per type: 'for (const type of lost) freeLead(player, [type], "fresh")' (line 417) and 'for (const type of emptied) freeLead(player, [type], "replacement")' (line 434). The first uncapped call defers the type and immediately calls flushPending, which sends a one-type message and sets lastSightingBoundary. The next type on the same tick is then capped and waits for the next boundary. Examples: two thefts in one batched view (skipped ticks are a design requirement); a theft of sun on the same tick that A's moon rumor goes stale while every copy of both is carried; two journal rumors emptied on one tick. In each case the player gets one type now and the other up to 30 s later. The flush at a boundary (line 415) also runs before that tick's losses and replacements (lines 417 and 434), so a trigger on the boundary tick itself misses the message going out on that tick and waits a further interval. This goes against decisions.md ('A player who lost two types learns about both at the next boundary, not one interval apart'). It also makes docs/intel.md wrong where it says 'two types that need a sighting at once are delivered together at the next boundary, not one interval apart' and 'a player who lost two types learns about both at once'. The property checker (property.test.ts checkPending) cannot catch this: it only requires delivery at the first boundary after the type was capped, and the second type is capped by the first type's message on the same tick. Suggested fix: collect every free carrier trigger of a player's step, including the boundary flush, into the pending set, then flush once. Add a scripted test for two uncapped losses (or a loss plus a replacement) on one tick.
findings.requirement: Its coverage reviewer blocked it on a real bug: a player with two deferred sightings got the second a whole interval late.

findings.message: A start trigger can produce a carrier sighting. freeLead(player, config.types, "start") (step.ts:401) defers every carried-only type and flushes, so a late joiner, or a start where every missing copy is carried, gets a carrier-sighting with reason 'start' that can list several types at once. The scripted test 'prefer a sealed source, then a cache, then a carrier sighting' (intel.test.ts) asserts this. features/intel-core/intel-task.md, which the task says still applies, says a carrier sighting 'is sent only on three triggers: a fresh rumor after a loss when every other copy is carried, a targeted rumor under the same condition, or a journal replacement when every remaining copy is carried'. This is inherited from the restored snapshot, but it is a spec deviation that is neither documented as a decision nor covered by EXERCISED, which lists only sighting:fresh, sighting:targeted and sighting:replacement.
findings.requirement: `features/intel-core/intel-task.md` and `features/intel-core/decisions.md` define the feature, and all of it still applies.
